title: .htaccess & Rewrite Rule Issues
description: Fix corrupted .htaccess breaking permalinks, causing 500 errors, or conflicting with plugin and server rewrite rules.

steps.title: Identify .htaccess Symptom
steps.instructions: Note if issue is 500 error, all pages 404, only certain URLs broken, or redirects not working. Check if Apache site (nginx sites use different config).

steps.title: Backup and Rename .htaccess
steps.instructions: Rename .htaccess to .htaccess.bak via SFTP. If site loads (without permalinks), .htaccess rules are the cause.

steps.title: Restore Default WordPress Rewrite Block
steps.instructions: Save Settings → Permalinks to regenerate default rules. Default block starts with # BEGIN WordPress and mod_rewrite rules for index.php.

steps.title: Audit Plugin-Added .htaccess Rules
steps.instructions: Cache, security, and redirect plugins add blocks above/below WordPress rules. Remove duplicate HTTPS redirects or conflicting RewriteRules one block at a time.

steps.title: Consolidate HTTPS Redirect Rules
steps.instructions: Multiple plugins and host may each add http→https redirects causing loops. Keep one canonical redirect layer (prefer server/host level).

steps.title: Verify AllowOverride on Server
steps.instructions: If permalinks save but URLs still 404, Apache may not allow .htaccess overrides. Contact host to enable AllowOverride All for the site directory.

steps.title: Translate Rules for Nginx (If Applicable)
steps.instructions: Nginx ignores .htaccess. Permalink rules must be in nginx site config. Provide host support the standard WordPress try_files block if needed.

steps.title: Verify Permalinks and Redirects
steps.instructions: Test posts, pages, categories, and custom redirects. Confirm no 500 errors and single canonical redirect from http to https.
